meta.name: Hangul Curriculum for Adaptive Quiz Engine
meta.description: Progressive Hangul curriculum from basic vowels through full syllable blocks with batchim.

lessons.title: Basic Vowels 1
lessons.description: The six simple vertical and horizontal vowels

pronunciation.ㅡ: eu (like the 'oo' in 'book'/'nook', but flatten your lips instead of rounding them — same tongue position, no lip rounding)

lessons.note: Important: a vowel can never be written by itself in Korean. Every syllable block needs something in the consonant slot, so when there's no real consonant sound, Korean fills that slot with 'ㅇ' as a silent placeholder. That's why ㅏ is always written 아, ㅓ is always written 어, and so on — you'll never see a bare vowel jamo standing alone in real text.

lessons.title: Basic Consonants 1
lessons.description: The five simplest consonants — no aspiration, no tension

pronunciation.ㄹ: r/l (flap r like 'tt' in 'butter', or l at end of syllable)

pronunciation.ㅅ: s/sh (s before ㅏㅓㅗㅜㅡㅐㅔ, sh before ㅣㅑㅕㅛㅠ)
pronunciation.ㅇ: silent at start of syllable, 'ng' at end (as in 'sing')

pronunciation.ㅊ: ch (as in 'cheese', aspirated — puff of air)

lessons.title: Syllable Blocks 1
lessons.description: Combining basic consonants and vowels into syllable blocks (CV pattern)
lessons.introduction: Hangul is written in syllable blocks. Each block has at least one consonant (C) and one vowel (V) in CV pattern. The consonant goes left or top, vowel goes right or bottom.

block_rules.vertical_layout: C on left, V on right (e.g., ㄱ + ㅏ = 가)
block_rules.horizontal_layout: C on top, V on bottom (e.g., ㄱ + ㅗ = 고)

lessons.title: Y-Vowels (Iotized Vowels)
lessons.description: Vowels with a 'y' sound added — formed by adding an extra stroke
lessons.formation: Each y-vowel is its base vowel (ㅏㅓㅗㅜ) with one extra stroke added
lessons.note: Reminder: like any vowel, a y-vowel can't stand alone — ㅑ is written 야, ㅕ is written 여, and so on, with the silent 'ㅇ' placeholder in front.

lessons.title: Compound Vowels 1
lessons.description: Vowels formed by combining two simple vowels

pronunciation.ㅔ: e (like 'e' in 'bed', slightly more closed — nearly identical in modern Seoul Korean)

lessons.note: In modern Seoul Korean, ㅐ and ㅔ sound nearly identical. Most Koreans can't hear the difference. This is the single most common spelling confusion for native speakers too. Reminder: these are still vowels, so written alone they always take the silent 'ㅇ' placeholder — ㅐ is written 애, ㅔ is written 에.

lessons.title: Compound Vowels 2
lessons.description: W-vowels — combining ㅗ or ㅜ with another vowel

pronunciation.ㅚ: oe (like 'we' in 'wet' — merged with ㅙ/ㅞ in modern Seoul Korean)
pronunciation.ㅢ: ui (like 'eu' + 'ee' — transitions from ㅡ to ㅣ)

lessons.note: ㅙ, ㅞ, and ㅚ are all pronounced identically in modern Seoul Korean. Learners don't need to distinguish them by ear, only by spelling. Reminder: written alone, these still take the silent 'ㅇ' placeholder — ㅘ is written 와, ㅝ is written 워, and so on.

lessons.title: Double Consonants (Tense)
lessons.description: Tense/double consonants — same shape, stronger articulation

pronunciation.ㄲ: kk (tense 'g/k' — tighten throat, no air puff)

lessons.note: Tense consonants are written by doubling the basic consonant. The throat muscles tighten — no puff of air escapes.

lessons.title: Final Consonants (Batchim) 1
lessons.description: Syllable-final consonants — the bottom position in a syllable block

batchim_pronunciation.ㄹ: l (tongue tip on ridge, like 'l' in 'bell')

lessons.note: Only 7 distinct sounds at the end of a syllable, even though many more consonants can appear there. This is the hardest concept for beginners — mastering it unlocks real Korean words.

lessons.title: Final Consonants (Batchim) 2
lessons.description: All remaining consonants in batchim position and their pronunciation rules

batchim_pronunciation_rules.ㄱㄲㅋㄳㄺ: all pronounced as ㄱ [k] in final position
batchim_pronunciation_rules.ㄷㅌㅅㅆㅈㅊㅎ: all pronounced as ㄷ [t] in final position
batchim_pronunciation_rules.ㅂㅍㄼㄿㅄ: all pronounced as ㅂ [p] in final position
batchim_pronunciation_rules.ㄴㄵㄶ: all pronounced as ㄴ [n] in final position
batchim_pronunciation_rules.ㄹㄽㄾㅀ: all pronounced as ㄹ [l] in final position
batchim_pronunciation_rules.ㅁㄻ: all pronounced as ㅁ [m] in final position
batchim_pronunciation_rules.ㅇ: pronounced as ㅇ [ng] in final position

lessons.note: Despite being written differently, many batchim sound identical. This is the #1 spelling challenge in Korean.

lessons.title: Reading Real Words
lessons.description: Apply everything: read multi-syllable Korean words with full batchim rules

quiz_modes.read_aloud: Show a Hangul letter/syllable, user pronounces it. Model scores accuracy.
quiz_modes.spell_it: Pronounce a syllable, user types the Hangul. Immediate right/wrong feedback.
quiz_modes.match_sound: Play audio or show romanization, user picks the correct Hangul from 4 choices.
quiz_modes.build_syllable: Give a pronunciation like 'ga', user assembles from consonant + vowel bank.
quiz_modes.sudden_death: Chain of increasingly hard questions. One wrong answer = session ends. Tracks streak.
quiz_modes.missing_vowel: Show consonant + romanization. User must type the correct vowel.
quiz_modes.batchim_challenge: Show a word missing its batchim. User must pick the correct final consonant.
quiz_modes.confusion_drill: Focus exclusively on letters the user consistently confuses. High-repetition, fast-paced.
